title: Google's November Android Update Fixes 216 Flaws, 23 of Them Critical
excerpt: The November 2026 security bulletin patches a zero-interaction remote code execution bug and an 'SMS of Death' flaw that can crash the calling service.
body:
• Google's November 2026 Android security bulletin, published November 2, fixes 216 vulnerabilities — 119 at patch level 2026-11-01 and 97 at 2026-11-05 — including 23 rated critical.
  • The most severe flaw, in the Framework component, could allow remote code execution with no user interaction and no extra privileges.
  • One critical flaw, nicknamed the "SMS of Death," lets a specially crafted text message crash Android's calling service, potentially interrupting emergency calls.
  • Check your phone's patch level under Settings > About phone > Android version: only patch level 2026-11-05 or later covers every fix in this bulletin.

Google has published its November 2026 Android security bulletin with fixes for 216 vulnerabilities, including 23 rated critical. The bulletin, published on November 2, is split across two patch levels: 2026-11-01 covers 119 issues in Android's Framework, System and Runtime components, and 2026-11-05 adds 97 more in the Linux kernel and in components from Arm, Imagination Technologies, MediaTek, Unisoc and Qualcomm.

The flaws that matter most

The most severe issue, Google says, is a critical vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed, and with no user interaction required for exploitation. Two further critical remote code execution flaws sit in media components: CVE-2026-58876, a use-after-free bug in Media Codecs, and CVE-2026-58936, a use-after-free in the libpng library's png_set_tRNS function; both carry CVSS scores of 9.8 in secondary analyses of the bulletin.

The most unusual entry is CVE-2026-58882, a critical denial-of-service flaw in the System component that researcher coverage has nicknamed the "SMS of Death." According to eSecurity Planet, specially crafted SMS messages can crash Android's calling service, potentially interrupting active calls, including emergency calls. The issue was disclosed publicly on October 29 by independent researcher Mark Blaszczyk, who had reported it to Google in May.

"Security patch levels of 2026-11-05 or later address all of these issues."

— Google, Android Security Bulletin, November 2026

Who is affected

The fixes span Android versions 14, 15, 16, 16-QPR2 and 17, with the exact set varying by vulnerability. The November bulletin contains no device-specific rollout dates: fixes reach phones through each manufacturer and carrier, and Google notes it notified its Android partners of all issues at least a month before publishing. Google has not flagged any issue in the bulletin as under exploitation in the wild.

Some fixes also arrive through Google Play system updates, which cover components such as Media Codecs, MediaProvider, Telephony and Wi-Fi. Samsung's November package, reported by eSecurity Planet citing SammyGuru, addresses 206 vulnerabilities in total, including 178 Android fixes from Google and 24 in Samsung's own software, though no firm rollout schedule was given.

What to do

Open Settings and check the security patch level shown under About phone > Android version — the exact path varies by maker. Pixel owners can check Settings for available system updates; Samsung users go to Settings > Software update > Download and install. Install the update as soon as your manufacturer offers it, and until the patch arrives, avoid opening media files from unknown senders. The full bulletin, with every CVE listed by component, is on the Android Open Source Project site.

For the hundreds of millions of Android users in India and across the diaspora — where Android is the default phone platform — the practical divide is between phones still receiving monthly patches and older devices that no longer do. A phone stuck below the 2026-11-05 patch level carries all 216 of these flaws unpatched, including the zero-interaction remote code execution bug.
